clue.text: His ideal place was in Fay Weldon's work

definitions.text: His ideal place was in Fay Weldon's work

parts.words: His ideal place was in Fay Weldon's work
parts.note: Fay Weldon wrote a novel titled after one man's utopia; the clue asks for the man whose ideal place it names

explanation.definitionFit: Weldon's 1990 novel is called Darcy's Utopia, a utopia being an ideal place.

clue.text: What a spade is called by Hammett

definitions.text: What a spade is called by Hammett

parts.words: What a spade is called by Hammett
parts.note: spade looks like a digging tool, but it is Sam Spade, Dashiell Hammett's private eye in The Maltese Falcon

explanation.definitionFit: Sam Spade is a private investigator, Hammett's archetypal sleuth.

clue.text: A mere version of Ouida

indicators.note: a new version of the words reworks their letters into another order

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a book as merely a copy of a Victorian novelist's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' rearranges A MERE. Ouida was the pen name of the novelist Maria Louise Ramé, who styled herself de la Ramée.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouida was the pen name of the novelist born Ramé, later calling herself de la Ramée.

clue.text: Prizewinning playwright — may be zany wit, OK?

indicators.note: the letters of the words that follow may be rearranged into the name wanted

explanation.surface: A playwright who wins prizes is asked whether a zany wit will do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges ZANY WIT and OK. Susan Yankowitz is an American playwright with several awards.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan Yankowitz is an award-winning American dramatist.

clue.text: He spent his time in reflection, ignoring echo, thus making a bloomer

definitions.text: He spent his time in reflection, ignoring echo, thus making a bloomer

parts.words: He spent his time in reflection, ignoring echo, thus making a bloomer
parts.note: the Greek youth gazed at his reflection in a pool, spurned the nymph Echo, and was turned into a flower, a bloomer, not a blunder

explanation.definitionFit: In myth the youth who loved his reflection and rejected Echo became the flower bearing his name.

clue.text: "One and simple man" emerging from the waves, we're told

definitions.text: "One and simple man" emerging from the waves, we're told

parts.words: "One and simple man" emerging from the waves, we're told
parts.note: the waves is Virginia Woolf's novel The Waves, and the quoted phrase is how one of its six speakers is described

explanation.definitionFit: Neville is one of the six voices in Woolf's The Waves.

clue.text: Young payback

definitions.meaning: Edward Young, poet of Night Thoughts
payback is retaliation for a wrong

explanation.definitionFit: Payback is retribution, getting even; Young's tragedy bears that title.

clue.text: Jerome journal for a man of leisure

definitions.meaning: Jerome K. Jerome co-edited the monthly magazine The ... in the 1890s
one who loafs about doing nothing

explanation.definitionFit: A loafer who does no work; also the title of Jerome's magazine.

clue.text: Title for coach of pseudonymous player

definitions.text: Title for coach of pseudonymous player

parts.words: Title for coach of pseudonymous player
parts.note: coach is a stagecoach, giving STAGE, and title gives NAME; together they are what an actor using a pseudonym performs under

explanation.definitionFit: An actor's professional pseudonym is the title they perform under.

clue.text: Poet heard to make threatening gesture with it

definitions.text: Poet heard to make threatening gesture with it

parts.words: Poet heard to make threatening gesture with it
parts.note: the playwright-poet's surname sounds like shake plus a weapon; brandishing that weapon is the threatening gesture

explanation.definitionFit: A spear is the weapon one shakes menacingly, as the bard's name suggests.

clue.text: Mr and Ms Eliot's Hastings play

definitions.text: Mr and Ms Eliot's Hastings play

parts.words: Mr and Ms Eliot's Hastings play
parts.note: Michael Hastings wrote a play named by the first names of T. S. Eliot and his first wife Vivienne

explanation.definitionFit: Hastings's 1984 play about the Eliots' marriage is titled with the couple's short first names.

clue.text: Did Mortimer's have too short a date?

definitions.text: Did Mortimer's have too short a date?

parts.words: Did Mortimer's have too short a date?
parts.note: Shakespeare's Sonnet 18 says summer's tenancy hath all too short a date; John Mortimer borrowed the phrase for his novel Summer's ...

explanation.definitionFit: A lease is a tenancy for a fixed term, the word in Mortimer's title Summer's Lease.

clue.text: "With his hypothesis and ultimate infallible " (Thomas Carlyle, Heroes)

definitions.text: "With his hypothesis and ultimate infallible " (Thomas Carlyle, Heroes)

parts.words: "With his hypothesis and ultimate infallible " (Thomas Carlyle, Heroes)
parts.note: the gap in Carlyle's sentence from On Heroes is filled by the Latin word for a statement of belief

explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a creed or set of beliefs, the word completing Carlyle's phrase.

clue.text: Aryan rule, possibly, for a shortish period

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A racial doctrine is said to have held sway only briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve lunar months make about 354 days, a little shorter than a calendar year.

clue.text: Just think of it repeated on Beckett cover

definitions.text: Just think of it repeated on Beckett cover

parts.words: Just think of it repeated on Beckett cover
parts.note: Beckett's short prose piece has a title in which one word appears twice, as Imagination Dead ... ; just think is the plain sense

explanation.definitionFit: To conceive of something in the mind is to picture it, the verb that ends Beckett's title.

clue.text: "That the —— are able to bear taxation is indubitable" (Samuel Johnson)

definitions.text: "That the —— are able to bear taxation is indubitable" (Samuel Johnson)

parts.words: "That the —— are able to bear taxation is indubitable" (Samuel Johnson)
parts.note: Johnson's pamphlet Taxation No Tyranny argued that the colonists across the Atlantic could pay their taxes

explanation.definitionFit: The colonists of the New World, the people of the United States, were Johnson's target.

clue.text: What the critics wrote about Edward Driffield, according to Maugham

definitions.text: What the critics wrote about Edward Driffield, according to Maugham

parts.words: What the critics wrote about Edward Driffield, according to Maugham
parts.note: Driffield is the novelist in Cakes and Ale whose critical praise Maugham treats as humbug

explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is nonsense or claptrap, which is how Maugham portrays the acclaim.

clue.text: Record of sensational occurrences in some beastly NNE wind

indicators.note: the letters wanted sit inside part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a diary of strange events during a nasty north-north-easterly gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in some' finds the title within bEASTLY NNE. Mrs Henry Wood's East Lynne was a famous Victorian sensation novel.
explanation.definitionFit: East Lynne (1861) is a classic sensation novel, full of melodramatic incident.

clue.text: Stand-in for Pericles

parts.note: in Shakespeare's Pericles, a lord governs Tyre while the prince is away

explanation.definitionFit: The loyal lord of Tyre deputises as ruler during the prince's wanderings.

clue.text: Ezra mistaken about field suggested for this high priest

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the next piece
a mistaken version of the name has its letters wrongly ordered

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow or field

explanation.surface: Ezra is wrong about a field that a priest proposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suggested' is only a link. ELEAZAR, Aaron's son, is the usual spelling; the grid's E in that unchecked square is a slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron's son succeeded him as chief priest of Israel.

clue.text: Incarnation of Lawrence in one composer

parts.note: T. E. Lawrence enlisted in the RAF under the assumed name Ross
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A biographer finds Lawrence of Arabia reborn as a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini wrote The Barber of Seville and other operas.

clue.text: Elkin book not a biography of a biographer

definitions.text: Elkin book not a biography of a biographer

parts.words: Elkin book not a biography of a biographer
parts.note: Stanley Elkin's first novel bears the surname of Johnson's famous biographer but is fiction about someone else

explanation.definitionFit: Elkin's 1964 novel shares its title with Johnson's biographer James Boswell.

clue.text: Very British type of McNeile hero

definitions.meaning: the dog breed is a symbol of British pluck
H. C. McNeile, writing as Sapper, created the adventurer Hugh Drummond

explanation.definitionFit: The breed stands for British tenacity; also Captain Drummond's nickname.

clue.text: Like Brooke's beauty

parts.note: Rupert Brooke's poetry speaks of beauty as common to all things

explanation.definitionFit: Something universal is found everywhere and belongs to all.

clue.text: First university demolished entirely for dramatist ()

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: entirely means all, completely

explanation.surface: An old college building is pulled down in full for a playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: The empty brackets in the clue as held presumably once held the play's title. Nicholas Udall wrote Ralph Roister Doister.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas Udall wrote the early English comedy Ralph Roister Doister.

clue.text: English distance covered by Rousseau?

parts.note: an imperial unit of length, 1,760 yards, stands for the distance

explanation.surface: A Frenchman asks whether Rousseau walked an English mile.
explanation.walkthrough: Rousseau's Émile is his treatise on education; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Émile is Rousseau's educational novel, so the title is a work by him.

clue.text: Carroll's game

parts.note: Lewis Carroll published The Game of ..., a book teaching syllogisms

explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's The Game of Logic taught formal reasoning through a board.

clue.text: Narayan's escort

definitions.meaning: R. K. Narayan's 1958 novel is about a tour leader named Raju

explanation.definitionFit: An escort shows travellers the way; also Narayan's novel title.

clue.text: Calculators from Ali Baba, cited in Chu Chin Chow

indicators.note: from shows the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Counting frames are taken from Ali Baba as quoted in the musical Chu Chin Chow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' finds the word within ali bABA CIted. Chu Chin Chow was a hit London musical based on Ali Baba.
explanation.definitionFit: Abacuses are bead frames used for counting, an early kind of calculator.

clue.text: Its reverse in literature is way out of line

definitions.text: Its reverse in literature is way out of line

parts.words: Its reverse in literature is way out of line
parts.note: setting a line in from the margin is the device; its opposite, a hanging line, sticks out of the line of text

explanation.definitionFit: Starting a line further in from the margin is called indenting.

clue.text: Paying attention in Albee piece

definitions.meaning: giving heed to what is said
Edward Albee wrote a 1976 radio play with this one-word title

explanation.definitionFit: Paying heed with one's ears; also an Albee play title.

clue.text: Lysander suggested his rival should marry him ()

definitions.text: Lysander suggested his rival should marry him ()

parts.words: Lysander suggested his rival should marry him ()
parts.note: in A Midsummer Night's Dream Lysander tells Demetrius he has Hermia's father's love, so do you marry him

explanation.definitionFit: Hermia's father in A Midsummer Night's Dream favours Demetrius as her husband.
